Original SASRec’s one-negative BCE baseline confounds loss choice with negative count when compared against full-catalog CE. The authors’ [controlled SASRec implementation](https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23) instead samples multiple unseen items per user and shares that set across sequence positions, supporting efficient candidate CE. However, uncorrected candidate CE, `logsumexp([s_pos, s_neg]) − s_pos`, remains a sampled-candidate objective; it does not equal full-catalog CE. [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) also identifies probability overconfidence under negative sampling, so neither more negatives nor a different loss guarantees better ranking on this benchmark.

For a controlled implementation comparison, keep architecture, batches, optimizer, training steps, temperature and sampled candidate IDs identical; vary only the loss. Sample uniformly without replacement from catalog IDs excluding padding and each user’s complete **training** history; cap K at the eligible pool size. Uniqueness prevents duplicate negatives from receiving repeated weight. Sharing negatives across positions preserves each position’s marginal sampling distribution but correlates its samples with other positions. Treat these as separate sampling ablations. For variable counts, mask invalid CE logits to `−inf`; for balanced multi-negative BCE use `softplus(−s_pos) + sum(mask * softplus(s_neg))/K_valid`, then average over valid sequence positions. Explicitly distinguish this from summed-negative BCE, whose positive/negative weighting changes with K. These are implementation recommendations, not measured RecHarness results. [TensorFlow’s sampled-softmax documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/compat/v1/nn/sampled_softmax_loss) additionally distinguishes accidental-hit removal and sampler expected-count corrections; removing target collisions alone does not exclude complete histories.
